subject: Warmseed micro-wave playbook — vectorstore quarantine & rerank acceptance
messages:
From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ian Brooks <ian.brooks@brightloop.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Warmseed micro-wave playbook — initial kickoff & vectorstore quarantine

Ian — following our SOW call, attaching a short playbook for the warmseed approach we discussed. Goal is to avoid a big bang backfill and instead run staggered micro-waves with a short "quarantine" period to surface mismatch/errors before traffic cutover.

High level plan (proposal):
- Wave 0 (warmseed): sample ~2% of active documents, push to vectorstore A and run rerank smoke tests. Quarantine for 48 hours to monitor retrieval drift and log errors.
- Micro-waves 1..N: each wave targets 10% dataset slices, with overlap windows for priming and replay.
- Acceptance gates: precision @10 > baseline -3%, rerank A/B neutral to +1% on CTR, no critical mapping errors for 48 hours.

Ask from BrightLoop: confirm the sample manifest schema (I attached CSV) and give us a preferred time window for Wave 0 (we recommend a low-traffic window).

Attachments: warmseed-sample-manifest.csv (schema + sampling seeds), rerank-eval-harness-spec.pdf (evaluation harness + thresholds).

Next steps:
1) BrightLoop agrees sampling window and gives an on-call for Wave 0.
2) Redwood runs warmseed and posts a short health summary (latency, recall, error-rate) to the shared Drive.

Thanks — I'll coordinate internal readiness once you confirm the window.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

From: Ian Brooks <ian.brooks@brightloop.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: BrightLoop Implementation <impl@brightloop.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Warmseed micro-wave playbook — initial kickoff & vectorstore quarantine

Thanks Soojin — this looks reasonable and I like the quarantine concept. A few clarifications from our side:

- Sampling: we can provide the CSV manifest you attached with the 2% seeds; will deliver by EOD (11th).
- Time window: we prefer a midnight–3am PST window for Wave 0 (low traffic).
- Vectorstore topology: we run a read-replica for testing, but we want to ensure index schema mapping is identical to prod. If Redwood needs a write-enabled endpoint for the warmseed, please confirm which host.

One risk we want to flag: our current enrichment pipeline occasionally adds fields that are not present in historical data — would the quarantine visibility catch field-mismatch errors (schema drift)? If not, we'll add a short enrichment hold for Wave 0.

We'll aim to get the manifest to you by EOD and assign Alicia (impl@brightloop.com) as the on-call.

— Ian
Ian Brooks
Head of Search Engineering, BrightLoop
ian.brooks@brightloop.com

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Warmseed micro-wave playbook — internal prep and QA checklist

Internal checklist before we sign off for Wave 0 (short bullets that map to our playbook):

- Priming: upload the warmseed KV entries and pre-populate model cache for the sample keys. Confirm cache TTL set to 6h for priming window.
- Vectorstore mapping: run the "schema-compare" job between testing replica and prod; log differences to the Drive. If new fields exist, we will mark them tolerated vs blocking in the manifest.
- Rerank harness: create a quick-run job with the attached spec; run 1k queries against warmseed slice and produce precision/recall and score-distribution plots.
- Monitoring: enable temporary traces for the warmseed cohort and a dedicated rerank log stream to capture score changes; wire a PagerDuty rule to an on-call (BrightLoop Alicia).
- Fallback policy: configure route that sends requests to the existing sparse baseline if the warmseed cluster exceeds 200ms median or error rate >0.5%.

I'll own the rerank harness run and will drop results into the Drive folder. Ben — can you take the schema-compare job and confirm we have suppressions for tolerated fields? Karthik — please draft the query set for the 1k-run (mix of head/long-tail).

Marissa
Director, Onboarding Ops | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Ian Brooks <ian.brooks@brightloop.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Warmseed micro-wave playbook — vectorstore quarantine & rerank acceptance

All set from my end — schema-compare run completed, attached a short CSV of tolerated mismatches (fields that are enrichment-only and safe to ignore). Key notes:

- No blocking mismatches found for the warmseed sample; five enrichment-only fields flagged as tolerated.
- I provisioned a write-enabled staging host for warmseed writes: vs-stage-03.redwood.internal (I'll share network ACL details in the Drive link).
- Rerank harness job queued for Wed 06:00 PST against the warmseed slice (1k queries). Output will include precision@10, recall@100, and score delta histogram.

Next checkpoints:
1) BrightLoop deliver manifest + Alicia on-call (by EOD today).
2) We run Wave 0 midnight–3am PST Thursday (14 Oct) and publish the 48h quarantine health summary Friday morning.

Attaching: warmseed-allowed-mismatches.csv (attachment stub).

— Ben
